title: Swe mid systemdesign read heavy scaling
topic: Swe mid systemdesign read heavy scaling
question: A social feed feature gets read thousands of times for every one time a post is written. How would you design the system to handle that read-heavy load without the database falling over?
idealAnswer:
Identifies read replicas as a core lever, routing feed reads to one or more read replicas while writes go to the primary, since the workload is overwhelmingly read-dominated

Proposes caching computed or frequently-read data (e.g. a user's feed, popular posts) rather than recomputing/querying it from scratch on every request

Addresses the write side too, even though it's lighter: writes still need to eventually be visible in reads, and a strong answer acknowledges replica lag as a real consequence of this design (a just-written post might not appear immediately)

Considers precomputing/denormalizing for read speed, e.g. a fan-out-on-write approach that pre-builds each follower's feed at post time, versus fan-out-on-read that assembles the feed at request time, and can explain the tradeoff between the two

Mentions indexing and query shape as a baseline, poorly indexed queries will hurt regardless of caching or replicas layered on top
